subject: maths

concepts.title: Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic
concepts.definition: Any integer greater than one can be broken down into a unique set of prime numbers, regardless of the sequence in which these factors are listed.
concepts.key_idea: Prime factorization is a unique signature for every composite number.
question_patterns: express the number as a product of prime factors
list the prime powers for the integer
decompose the composite number into primes
write the prime product representation of

solution_steps.explain: Find the smallest prime that divides the number and record it.

concepts.title: HCF and LCM via Prime Factorization
concepts.definition: The highest common factor is the product of the lowest powers of common prime factors, while the least common multiple is the product of the highest powers of all prime factors present.
concepts.key_idea: Use prime powers to extract shared and total factors.
question_patterns: calculate the HCF and LCM of two numbers
find the least common multiple using prime factorization
determine the highest common factor for the pair
verify the product of two numbers equals their HCF times LCM
compute the LCM given the HCF and two numbers

solution_steps.explain: Divide the product by the HCF to isolate LCM.

concepts.title: Irrationality of Square Roots
concepts.definition: Numbers that cannot be expressed as a ratio of two integers, such as the square root of any prime, are irrational.
concepts.key_idea: Proof by contradiction using the Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic.
question_patterns: prove that the square root is irrational
show that the number is not rational
verify why the root cannot be written as p/q
explain the contradiction in assuming the root is rational

solution_steps.explain: Start by assuming the number equals a fraction.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Find LCM of {a} and {b} given HCF is {hcf}
